title: Alzheimer’s disease rewires gene coexpression networks coupling different brain regions
authors: Mitra S; B P K; C R S; Saikumar NV; Philip P; Narayanan M
one_liner_zh: 该研究基于RNA-seq进行跨脑区差异共表达网络分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，且未采用AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Connectome studies have revealed how neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupt functional and structural connectivity among brain regions, but the molecular basis of such disruptions is less studied, with most genomic studies focusing on within-brain-region molecular analyses. We performed an inter-brain-region differential correlation (DC) analysis of postmortem human brain RNA-seq data available for four brain regions – frontal pole, superior temporal gyrus, parahippocampal gyrus, and inferior frontal gyrus – from Mount Sinai Brain Bank for hundreds of AD vs. control samples. For any two brain regions, our DC analysis identifies all pairs of genes across these regions whose coexpression/correlation strength in the AD group differs significantly from that in the Control group, after adjusting for cell type compositional effects to better capture cell-intrinsic changes. Such DC gene pairs provided information complementary to known differentially expressed genes in AD, and highlighted extensive rewiring of the network of cross-region coexpression-based couplings among genes. The most vulnerable region in AD, parahippocampal gyrus, showed the most rewiring in its coupling with other brain regions. Decomposing the DC network into bipartite (region-region) gene modules revealed enrichment for synaptic signaling and ion transport pathways in several modules, revealing the dominance of five genes ( BSN, CACNA1B, GRIN1, IQSEC2 , and SYNGAP1 ). AD cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers (AD-CSF), neurotransmitters, secretory proteins, ligand and receptors were found to be part of the DC network, suggesting how pathways comprising such signaling molecules could mediate region-region communication. A module enriched for AD GWAS (Genome-wide Association Studies) signals is also enriched for NF-κβ signaling pathway, a key mediator of brain inflammation in AD. Beyond modules, we also identified individual genes that act as hubs of AD dysregulation across regions, such as ZKSCAN1 (Zinc Finger with KRAB And SCAN Domains) – this gene is known to be linked to AD in GWAS studies but via unknown mechanisms, and the specific DC interactions of ZKSCAN1 found in this study can be used to dissect these mechanisms. Thus, our inter-region DC framework provides a valuable new perspective to comprehend AD aetiology.
abstract_zh: 连接组学研究已揭示神经退行性疾病如阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer’s disease, AD）如何破坏大脑区域间的功能性和结构性连接，但这些破坏的分子基础研究较少，大多数基因组学研究集中于脑区内分子分析。我们对来自西奈山脑库（Mount Sinai Brain Bank）的四个脑区——额极（frontal pole）、颞上回（superior temporal gyrus）、海马旁回（parahippocampal gyrus）和额下回（inferior frontal gyrus）——的死后人脑RNA-seq数据进行了脑区间差异相关（differential correlation, DC）分析，涵盖数百个AD与对照样本。对于任意两个脑区，我们的DC分析识别出这些区域间所有基因对，其共表达/相关强度在AD组与对照组中存在显著差异，并在调整细胞类型组成效应以更好捕捉细胞内在变化后进行。此类DC基因对提供了与AD中已知差异表达基因互补的信息，并突显了跨区域共表达耦合基因网络的广泛重连。AD中最脆弱的区域——海马旁回——在与其他脑区的耦合中显示出最多的重连。将DC网络分解为二分（区域-区域）基因模块，揭示了多个模块中突触信号传导和离子转运通路的富集，并显示出五个基因（BSN、CACNA1B、GRIN1、IQSEC2和SYNGAP1）的主导作用。AD脑脊液生物标志物（AD-CSF）、神经递质、分泌蛋白、配体和受体被发现是DC网络的一部分，提示包含此类信号分子的通路可能介导区域间通讯。一个富集AD GWAS（全基因组关联研究）信号的模块也富集了NF-κβ信号通路，这是AD脑炎症的关键介质。除模块外，我们还识别出作为AD跨区域失调枢纽的单个基因，如ZKSCAN1（含KRAB和SCAN结构域的锌指蛋白）——该基因在GWAS研究中已知与AD相关，但机制未知，本研究中发现的ZKSCAN1特定DC相互作用可用于解析这些机制。因此，我们的区域间DC框架为理解AD病因学提供了有价值的新视角。
